“For me, the NASDAQ is the market … when the 10 day is rising and the 20 day is rising and when the 10 day is above the 20 day. Okay? That's a momentum market.” (Swing Trading School, 4 Aug 2020) · “I mostly use QQQs … you can use like a green light, yellow light, red light, kind of a filter on the markets” (18 May 2023)

Rule (desk): Rulebook §7 / §11.0 [NEW 10-05]. Lead index = QQQ (“For me, the NASDAQ is the market”, STS 4 Aug 2020). GREEN light = AGGRESSIVE: 10-day SMA above the 20-day SMA and both rising (slope vs 5 sessions ago), his “momentum market”. RED = CASH: 10 below 20 and both falling: no breakout longs, only A+ EPs on huge volume at reduced size. YELLOW = SELECTIVE: anything in between: A+ only, half size. IWM is the small-cap check: names under $2B use the weaker of QQQ and IWM, and small-cap EPs need IWM at least YELLOW. SPY is shown for reference only (“I couldn't care less about S&P 500”).

Trigger = the range high. Live entry = the break of the first 5-minute candle high (ORH) through it (a buy-stop at the range high if it opens below). If the stock gaps well above the trigger, re-plan instead of chasing. Stop shown = the tighter of last session's low and Trigger − 1 ADR; on the day, use the actual low of the day, and skip the trade if that is more than 1 ADR away. Max sh = 1% of the 20-session average share volume (his liquidity cap); size by risk first, then cap. Trail = his MA by size: micro / small caps on the 10-day, large caps on the 20-day (mid caps: 10-day if ADR ≥ 5%). NOT A BUY rows stay on the page but are held back from Setup Master: earnings within 3 sessions of the next session (2026-10-12), a small-cap biotech breakout, or a red light for that size. Q = 0–100 desk score: momentum rank 20, tightness 20, consolidation length 10, MA surf 15, distance to trigger 15, volume dry-up 10, ADR 5, prior move 5. Earnings dates come from yfinance (unverified) unless Equity Research has confirmed them. Check them before entry.

Catalyst = an earnings date (SEC XBRL, desk fundamentals feed) or an 8-K/6-K filed within 3 days of the gap. The headline itself is not read unless the source is marked hand-checked. "Pre 3M" = gain over the 3 months before the gap. Low = neglected stock, which makes the better EP. Trigger = the high since the EP. Stop = the tighter of last session's low and Trigger − 1.5 ADR (his EP cap). Tier KK = his $100M day; desk tier = ≥$20M on ≥3x volume (the desk's fallback for smaller names, page only, not sent to Setup Master). A = gap ≥10%. Cards: A-grade (gap ≥10%) at his $vol that held the EP-day low first, earnings EPs ahead of news EPs (“I mostly trade earnings EPs”), then most recent. Only those with a found catalyst go to Setup Master (rulebook §11.2). Live entry = “wait for the first, say, five minute candle”, buy the break of its high, stop at the low of the day. Biotech EPs are not excluded (“I absolutely don't avoid biotech EPs they're the best”); the small-cap-biotech caution is for breakouts. Small-cap EPs (under $2B) are held back while IWM is red. Max sh = 1% of the 20-session average share volume.

Rulebook §8.1A. Growth = close ÷ lowest low of the last 22 / 65 / 126 bars (his formula; 126 for 6M confirmed in his Aug 2020 stream, rulebook §8.1-E). Rank = percentile across every NYSE / Nasdaq / NYSE American common stock and ADR at $5 or more. "10MA in ADR" = distance above the 10-day SMA in ADR units: above about +2 is stretched, 0 to +1 is surfing. Click a header to sort. Tap a row to open the desk stock page.

THE METHOD verified rules only, with sources

Setups

  • Breakout: a big move (30–100%+) in the past 1–3 months. Then an orderly pullback with higher lows and a tightening range, usually 2 weeks to 2 months, surfing the rising 10/20-day MA. Then a range expansion. [1]
  • Episodic pivot: unexpected news gaps the stock 10%+ on big volume. Best when the stock had not already rallied for 3–6 months. A gap that sells off is not an EP. [1] [2] By 2023 EPs were his main setup: “for me most of the EPs I trade they are gap ups of 10% plus” and “I mostly trade earnings EPs, because those are the ones you get most of.” [12] Earnings EPs sort first here.
  • Biotech: biotech EPs are allowed (“I absolutely don't avoid biotech EPs they're the best”). [12] The “avoid the small cap biotechs” line was about breakouts [11], so small-cap biotech breakouts are held back here.

His scans (run here)

  • Momentum: 1-day dollar volume over $150M, ADR% (20) over 3.5, ranked on close ÷ lowest low of 22 bars (1M), 65 bars (3M) and 126 bars (6M), top 90% band, tightened to 95% above 50 hits. [3] The 126-day 6M window is his (Aug 2020 stream).
  • EP: up more than 7.5% on the day, close above yesterday's high, over $100M traded. [4] The ticker check then wants a 10%+ gap and real news. [2]

Entry & stop

  • Breakouts: buy the opening-range high as the stock breaks out: “the highs of the first one minute candle, the first five minute candle or the first 60 minute candle”. The desk default is the first 5-minute candle. [1] [9]
  • EPs: “Just wait for the first, say, five minute candle”, buy when it takes out that high, stop at the low of the day. [12]
  • Stop = low of the day, no wider than 1× ADR on breakouts, at most 1.5× on EPs. [1] [2]
  • Earnings: “I would recommend you never buy stocks like let's say within three days of earnings.” [10] No new breakout buy within 3 sessions before a report; those rows are marked NOT A BUY. Dates are yfinance (unverified) unless confirmed.
  • On this page, Trigger = the range high (EP: the high since the gap). The plan stop is the tighter of the last session's low and Trigger − 1 ADR (EPs 1.5 ADR). Once live, the stop is the entry day's low.

Sizing

  • Risk 0.25–1% of the account per trade, rarely more than 1%. [1]
  • Most positions are 10–20% of the account. Never hold more than 30% in one stock overnight. [1]
  • Liquidity cap: “you don't want to be more than 1% of the average daily volume of a stock.” [12] Max sh on each card = 1% of the 20-session average share volume. Size by risk first, then cap.

Selling

  • Sell 1/3–1/2 after 3–5 days and move the stop to break-even. [1]
  • Trail the rest on the 10- or 20-day MA and exit on the first close below it. [1] [8] By size: “micro caps could be, you know, ten days”, and “when it large caps it's always the 20 day”. [14] “the 20 works better on like larger cap stocks.” [13]
  • Trail on each card: micro / small caps (under $2B) 10-day; large caps ($10B+) 20-day; mid caps 10-day if ADR ≥ 5%, else 20-day (desk reading of “depends on how fast the stock is”). A 200%+ run in 10 sessions says “sell into strength” instead. [14]

Market

  • “For me, the NASDAQ is the market.” 10-day rising, 20-day rising and the 10 above the 20 = “a momentum market”. With the 10 below the 20 and both falling, “you probably shouldn't trade swing trade on the long side.” [9]
  • His own traffic-light framing: “I mostly use QQQs … you can use like a green light, yellow light, red light, kind of a filter on the markets.” In bad periods “you either do fewer trades or you do smaller size.” [12]
  • Here: GREEN = Aggressive, YELLOW = Selective (A+ only, half size), RED = Cash (no breakout longs) on QQQ. IWM is the small-cap check: names under $2B use the weaker light, and small-cap EPs need IWM at least yellow (rulebook §7, §11.0). SPY is shown for reference only. [6] [7] [8]

Where the desk deviates

  • Price ≥ $5 (he trades lower). Breakout watch uses the desk liquidity floor (ADV $20M, §11.1) because volume dries up in a flag; his $150M is a 1-day scan filter.
  • If a momentum window has fewer than 20 hits at $150M, it drops to his May 2020 floor ($60M), then $20M, and says so.
  • EPs from the last 10 sessions stay on watch. A desk tier (≥$20M on ≥3× volume) shows smaller names on the page only.
  • Market-cap bands (micro <$300M, small <$2B, large ≥$10B), “A+” = Q ≥ 80, “huge volume” = ≥5× and the session count for earnings (weekdays less NYSE holidays) are desk choices. Market caps come from cached Massive ticker details.
  • Not automated: his “breakouts and breakdowns both failing” overlay and the 30-open-positions tell. Check those by eye.
